description: Before the fix, `bench/corpus/BC-*.json` could carry a `documented_in` string pointing at a nonexistent test class or function -- a rename or deletion in `tests/` left the corpus row stale and nothing fired. Operators reading the corpus to plan adversarial coverage got false reassurance that a class was tested when its regression had silently rotted away. Fix: parametrized AST resolver test in `tests/test_corpus_documented_in_resolves.py` that walks every in-scope corpus row and asserts the referenced test resolves to a real class or function in the named test file. Combo refs (` + `, `; `, ` plus `) and parenthetical annotations are tolerated; BC-OOS-* rows are excluded because they document out-of-scope bypasses without a harness-side test.

canonical_attempts.intended_target: operator plants a corpus row whose documented_in points at a nonexistent test file
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: AST resolver returns False; parametrized test fails the assertion naming the unresolvable ref

canonical_attempts.intended_target: test file exists but the named class was renamed; corpus row is stale
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: AST symbol set does not contain the stale name; resolver returns False
